scope: Proposition 13.5 (Full solid boxes with a height guard) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 63. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let the source and target families be finite collections of full rational axis-aligned solid boxes, each family pairwise disjoint. Write their centers as ai, bi and their positive half-widths as ri,j, wi,j. Require each prescribed affine map to send its entire source box onto its specified target box: Fi(ai + h) = bi + Dih, Di = diag(wi,1/ri,1, wi,2/ri,2, wi,3/ri,3), det Di = 1. Suppose every source center has height at most −1, and every target center has height at most −1 or exactly 1. They admit an effective compactly supported solenoidal unit-time realization. If a target center has negative height, every point ai + h of its source box with h3 = 0 remains at negative height throughout. A rational bound for the entire support is computable from the boxes.
